title: LNG Freight Rates Surge By 50% As Europe Races To Refill Inventories
summary: A month ago, global exports of liquefied natural gas hit an all-time high. They’re about to grow further, however, as winter in the northern hemisphere draws nearer and demand for heating soars. The first signs are already showing: LNG tanker rates are surging, gaining over 50% in the past week. A week ago, the average daily rate for a 174,000-cu m LNG carrier crossing the Atlantic stood at $39,750, Reuters reported, citing figures from pricing data provider Spark Commodities. This Monday, that daily average had surged to $61,750, before…

title: U.S. Natural Gas Futures Skyrocket on Record LNG Export Demand
summary: Cold, dry Arctic air moving across the central and eastern US early next week will cause temperatures to drop to 10-15 degrees below average, according to the Weather Prediction Center. The chilly forecast is causing natural gas prices to spike, as the demand for heating fuel increase,s as it normally does this time of year.  Natural gas now provides about 40% of US electricity.  U.S. natural gas futures on Monday climbed above $4.30 per MMBtu, the highest since March. title: U.S. LNG Exports Break 100 Million Tons in Record 2025
summary: U.S. liquefied natural gas exports set new records in 2025 as new capacity came online and existing terminals ran at high utilization, pushing annual shipments past levels previously thought years away. Preliminary data from LSEG show the United States exported 111 million metric tons of LNG last year, making it the first country to surpass the 100-million-ton threshold in a single year. title: Inside Brazil’s Race to Secure Gas Supply
summary: TAG is the gas transmission operator responsible for the main transport corridor connecting Cabiunas, Brazil (Point I), the biggest gas injection point in the country, located from Rio de Janeiro to Ceara (Point O). TAG will play a central role in integrating new domestic gas supply from the Sergipe Alagoas deepwater project (SEAP), liquefied natural gas (LNG) entry points, and demand centers across Brazil’s Southeast and Northeast regions.
